oneLiner: The database incumbent that bet the balance sheet on AI infrastructure: a $664B backlog and 121% OCI growth set against negative free cash flow, $125B of debt, a $20B equity raise, and a stock still down roughly 59% from its 2025 high.
thesis: The backlog is real and still growing. RPO reached $664B at Q1 FY27 (quarter ended Aug 31, 2026, reported Sep 10, 2026), up $209B YoY and $26B QoQ, after more than $30B of new AI cloud contracts that management says require no additional Oracle capital.

Conversion has visibly started. OCI revenue rose 121% YoY to $7.4B in Q1 FY27 (from 93% in Q4 FY26), total revenue grew 30% to $19.35B, and Oracle delivered 850MW of new capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs since the end of Q4. FY27 guidance was nudged up to at least $90B of revenue and $8.10 of non-GAAP EPS.

The bet is still externally funded, which is the whole controversy. Q1 FY27 capex was $28.5B against $23.1B of operating cash flow (itself flattered by $11.4B of customer prepayments), so free cash flow was negative $5.4B; Oracle sold $20B of stock via its ATM program in the quarter and carries about $125B of notes and borrowings (Aug 31, 2026).

Customer concentration cuts both ways. Roughly $300B of the backlog is attributed by press reports to OpenAI/Stargate (not company-confirmed). A late-Sept 2026 report of OpenAI's revenue run-rate nearing $70B lifted the stock, but a force majeure notice on the New Mexico Stargate campus shows the physical buildout risk.

The de-rating has already happened. At $142.30 (Oct 2, 2026 close) ORCL trades near 17.6x the $8.10 FY27 EPS guide, below the 23-27x range cited for MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, and META, despite far faster contracted growth.

latestProse: Oracle's fiscal Q1 FY27 (reported Sep 10, 2026) was the first quarter in which the backlog visibly turned into revenue at scale: total revenue rose 30% to $19.35B, OCI grew 121% to $7.4B, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.92 beat consensus near $1.73-1.75 by roughly 10%. GAAP operating income jumped 57% to $6.7B and the non-GAAP margin held at 42%, easing fears that low-margin GPU rental would crush profitability. RPO rose a more modest $26B to $664B, with management stressing that the new contracts carry no incremental capital need. The cash picture improved but did not flip: $23.1B of operating cash flow, swollen by $11.4B of customer prepayments, still fell short of $28.5B of capex, and the gap was bridged by a $20B at-the-market stock sale that lifted the diluted share count to 3.0B. Shares rose roughly 7% after the print (per a report citing CNBC) but gave it back by early October amid data-center delay headlines. The disclosure that matters most: $11.4B of Q1 operating cash flow came from customer prepayments, meaning the headline cash improvement depends on counterparties funding Oracle's buildout up front rather than on the business paying for itself.
guidanceProse: For Q2 FY27 Oracle guided total revenue growth of 30-34%, cloud revenue growth of 65-71% in USD, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.85-1.93 (up 21-25% excluding the one-time Ampere gain in Q2 FY26). For the full year it now expects revenue of at least $90B (previously about $90B, up 34% in constant currency) and non-GAAP EPS of $8.10 (previously $8.05). The financing plan is unchanged: roughly $40B of FY27 debt and equity, of which the $20B ATM is now done, no further debt expected in calendar 2026, and a $70B FY27 net capex outlay guide from June (not restated in the Q1 release). Management says infrastructure revenue acceleration, now nine consecutive quarters, should continue through FY27. Any slip in data-center power delivery flows straight into the leverage story.

guide.label: FY27 outlook (raised Sep 10, 2026)
guide.sub: Q2 FY27: revenue +30-34%, cloud +65-71%, EPS $1.85-1.93; ~$40B FY27 financing ($20B ATM done); $70B net capex outlay guide (Jun 2026)

segments: Cloud infrastructure (OCI): $7.4B in Q1 FY27, up 121% YoY (CPU/GPU $6.5B, up 151%; database services $0.9B, up 26%); the growth engine, capital-hungry during the buildout
Cloud applications (Fusion, NetSuite, Industry incl. Oracle Health): $4.2B in Q1 FY27, up 10% YoY; the steady, high-margin SaaS base
Legacy license, support, hardware, and services: software revenue $5.55B in Q1 FY27, down 3%; slow-shrinking, but still the cash cow funding the transition
competitive: MSFT/Azure: larger and self-funded from internal cash flow; Oracle is the only hyperscaler-scale builder financing capex with debt, equity issuance, and customer prepayments
AMZN/AWS: the scale leader that Oracle undercuts on large GPU-cluster pricing and network interconnect; AWS grows a fraction as fast as OCI's 121% (Q1 FY27), but off a vastly larger base
GOOGL/GCP: the closest analog in using AI demand to gain infrastructure share, but with a fortress balance sheet behind it
SAP: the applications rival relevant to Fusion and NetSuite, and entirely absent from the AI infrastructure land grab
Neoclouds (CoreWeave and peers): compete for the same AI training contracts with even more aggressive debt structures, and set the marginal price of GPU capacity
moat: The database franchise and the enterprise install base are a genuine moat with decades of switching costs, and they fund everything else. OCI's edge, price-performance on large GPU clusters and a willingness to build to a single customer's specification, is an execution advantage rather than a structural one; commodity GPUs plus outside capital is a replicable formula. The $664B backlog is contractual protection, but its value is only as good as the counterparties behind it and Oracle's ability to energize sites on time.
risks: OpenAI concentration: reportedly around $300B of RPO depends on one unprofitable counterparty's ability to keep raising capital

Leverage and dilution: notes and borrowings about $125B (Aug 31, 2026), debt rated BBB- by S&P (per Business Chief), and a $20B equity sale in Q1 FY27 that lifted diluted shares 3% YoY; a credit shock raises the cost of the whole strategy (CNBC flagged rising bond-yield risk for debt-funded data-center builders, Sep 27, 2026)
Negative free cash flow persists: negative $23.7B in FY26 and negative $5.4B in Q1 FY27 even after $11.4B of customer prepayments; prepayment-funded cash flow can reverse

Power and construction delays: a force majeure notice on the New Mexico Stargate campus (Project Jupiter) and an Aterio warning that the 1.3GW Port Washington, Wisconsin campus may miss its 2H 2027 target on grid approval (Sept 2026)
Asset obsolescence and margin mix: GPUs depreciate fast (Q1 FY27 depreciation $3.2B vs $1.4B a year earlier); data centers built for today's chips risk aging out before contracts fully monetize
TikTok entanglement: the 15% stake in the TikTok USDS joint venture (valued near $2B in a Mar 2026 filing) adds geopolitical exposure disproportionate to its financial size
catalysts: Oracle AI World, Las Vegas, Oct 25-28, 2026, with Investor Day on Oct 28: likely update on multi-year targets, capex, and new contracts
Fiscal Q2 FY27 earnings (expected around Dec 9, 2026, date unverified): test of the 65-71% cloud growth guide and RPO-to-revenue conversion
Remaining FY27 financing (about $20B left of the ~$40B plan; no new debt expected in calendar 2026): timing, mix, and rating-agency reaction
Data-center energization milestones: New Mexico (Project Jupiter) gas supply and Wisconsin (Port Washington) grid approval
OpenAI/Stargate funding and revenue updates through 2026-27: each one de-risks or re-risks a large share of the backlog
pricedIn: At $142.30 (Oct 2, 2026 close), ORCL trades near 17.6x the $8.10 FY27 EPS guide, with a market cap around $409B: cheaper than MSFT, GOOGL, and its own recent history, for a company guiding 30%-plus revenue growth. The stock sits about 59% below its September 2025 high of $345.68 and near the low end of its 52-week range ($114.50-$322.54). A roughly 7% post-earnings pop faded within weeks on New Mexico and Wisconsin delay headlines, so the market is still refusing to pay for the beat. Priced in: negative free cash flow through FY27, continued dilution, and meaningful OpenAI counterparty risk. Not priced in: either a clean RPO-to-revenue conversion with margins holding near 42% non-GAAP, or a counterparty or power failure that strands the capex. Consensus target and rating as of Oct 2026: unverified.

scenarios.bear: OpenAI's funding stumbles in 2027 and Stargate buildouts slip on power delays; portions of RPO are re-termed or cancelled while capex is already committed. Prepayment inflows dry up, free cash flow deepens, and further equity issuance dilutes holders while rating agencies act on a debt stack already near $125B. EPS undershoots the $8.10 guide and the equity re-rates on stressed earnings: 12-13x on roughly $7 of EPS points back toward the $90-110 range, below the 52-week low.
scenarios.base: The backlog converts on schedule but unevenly: FY27 revenue lands at or slightly above $90B with EPS near $8.10, free cash flow stays negative through FY27 and approaches breakeven in FY28 as early data centers reach full contractual contribution. The remaining ~$20B of financing is placed without a downgrade. The multiple recovers modestly to 21-23x forward as conversion evidence accumulates, supporting a $170-185 stock over 12 months, earned quarter by quarter against the leverage clock.
scenarios.bull: AI training and inference demand stays supply-constrained, OpenAI keeps raising capital, and Oracle signs further non-OpenAI mega-deals that dilute concentration risk. OCI growth stays above 100% into FY28, non-GAAP margins hold in the low 40s on 98% utilization and renewal premiums, and free cash flow turns positive earlier than feared. EPS runs toward $10-11 by FY28 and the market re-pays a mid-20s multiple on a de-risked backlog: a $250-plus stock.
